note: Independent HEAD re-judgment against RFC 7606 Section 5.1: "Since older BGP speakers may not implement these restrictions, an implementation MUST still be prepared to receive these fields in any position or combination." Verified the {single-polarity: positive} annotation: rejecting any permitted combination solely for sender restrictions would violate this receiver obligation. Read all eight tagged carriers (TestRFC7606Section51AcceptsMPUnreachAfterOtherAttributes, TestRFC7606Section51AcceptsReachAndUnreachTogether, TestRFC7606Section51AcceptsMPReachWithLegacyNLRI, TestRFC7606Section51AcceptsMPUnreachWithLegacyNLRI, TestRFC7606MPReachIPv4NextHopValid, test/plugin/rfc7606-receive-combinations.ci, test/plugin/rfc7606-relay-one-field.ci, and checkRFC7606MixedUpdate delegating to checkMixedUpdateWire) plus producer applyRFC7606. All five Go units assert RFC7606ActionNone for trailing MP attributes and mixed combinations; both .ci tests verify live-daemon acceptance, relay delivery, and absence of Error NOTIFICATIONs; checkMixedUpdateWire verifies real FRR interop with seeded withdrawal, announcement installation, exact split wire capture, and surviving session. Changes since the prior audit (next-hop unchanged in rfc7606-relay-one-field.ci and edits to an unrelated function in check_rfc.go) preserved every receive-acceptance assertion. Source re-judgment only; no test or gate run claimed.
